$schema_note: Source of truth for the GitHub repository rulesets. Apply via .github/workflows/apply-branch-protection.yml, or by running tools/apply_branch_protection.py directly. Schema follows the GitHub REST API: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets. This file holds a LIST of rulesets under `rulesets`; the reconciler handles each one by name.
$model: Branching: feature -> dev (PR) -> main (promotion workflow only).
dev is the integration branch: every merge lands there first and CI runs on it.
main is the released branch. It moves only via .github/workflows/promote-to-main.yml,
which fast-forwards it to a dev commit that has already gone green, plus the
version-bump commit release-cli.yml writes.
MERGE RIGHTS. Merging a PR requires write access, and write is granted to exactly two
collaborators: 0x-copilot-dev and parthpahwa1. Anyone may fork and open a PR; nobody
else can merge one. That is enforced by repository access, not by these rules --
a ruleset cannot express 'only these logins may merge'. Keep the collaborator list
short and this property holds.
REVIEWS. Outside contributors need 2 approvals, which with two collaborators means
both must approve. The two collaborators are bypass actors, so their own PRs need no
review. Bypass is the only mechanism GitHub offers for an author-dependent review
requirement -- there is no per-author review count.
CHECK CONTEXTS are CHECK-RUN NAMES: bare job names, carrying the matrix suffix where a
job is a matrix (e.g. 'cli (ubuntu-latest)'). They are NOT 'workflow / job'. That form
is only how the PR UI renders them; used here it silently matches nothing and leaves
every PR blocked forever on a check that never reports. Verify any addition against:
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/SHA/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[].name'
REQUIRED CHECKS ARE DELIBERATELY FEW. Every workflow here is path-filtered, and GitHub
treats a required check that never runs as pending, blocking the PR. So only
unconditional checks belong in this list. The per-service suites (ci-ai-backend,
ci-backend, ci-backend-facade, ci-frontend, ci-desktop, ci-cli) are NOT required per-PR
for exactly that reason -- promote-to-main.yml gates them instead, evaluating the whole
commit rather than one PR's diff. That is the stronger gate: it is what would have
caught the ci-desktop and ci-e2-final-conformance breakage that reached main.
required_signatures is deliberately ABSENT. Most history is unsigned (verify with
`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits --jq '.[].commit.verification.verified'`), so enabling
it blocks all work. Turn it on only as part of a deliberate signing rollout.
WHY main CARRIES FEWER RULES THAN dev. This looks backwards until you try the
alternative. Review and checks live on dev, and main only ever receives commits that
already passed them -- so repeating the rules on main adds nothing and breaks the
promotion path, because the two workflows that legitimately move main cannot satisfy
them:
* A `pull_request` rule blocks promote-to-main.yml's fast-forward outright.
* `required_status_checks` blocks release-cli.yml's version-bump commit, which is new
and therefore has no checks of its own.
The usual escape is a GitHub Actions bypass actor (actor_type Integration, id 15368).
That is UNAVAILABLE here: the API rejects it with "Actor GitHub Actions integration
must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization" -- Integration bypass actors
require an ORG, and this repo is owned by a user. Same root cause as the CODEOWNERS
teams problem.
required_linear_history is ABSENT from main for the same family of reason, found the
same way -- by running the promotion for real. It forbids merge commits, and every PR
merged into dev creates one, which promotion then fast-forwards onto main:
remote: - This branch must not contain merge commits.
remote:   Found 1 violation: e9fe1436 (Merge pull request #474)
The rule is structurally incompatible with this branching model. The alternative --
squash-only merges into dev -- would make dev linear and satisfy it, but it would also
collapse each PR to a single commit, and tools/cli_release.py builds the changelog from
the individual Conventional Commits inside a PR (it already skips merge commits with
--no-merges). Squashing would coarsen every release note to one line per PR. main also
already contains merge commits throughout its history, so the rule was aspirational,
never enforced.
So main keeps the rules that protect it without blocking its own workflows -- no
deletion, no force-push -- and its QUALITY gate is promote-to-main.yml,
which refuses to promote a dev commit whose checks are not all green and not all
finished. That evaluates the whole commit rather than one diff, which is the stronger
check anyway. The residual risk is honest and worth naming: a collaborator CAN still
push directly to main. Nothing here prevents that; only the two-person collaborator
list does. Moving the repo into an organization would restore the bypass actor and let
the stricter rules come back.
